structures.name: Contractile vacuole
structures.evidence: It swims in a spiral, and two contractile vacuoles, each ringed by 6 to 10 canals, sit near its front and back ends.

sources.title: Paramecium caudatum: Habitat, Culture, Structure, Locomotion

structures.name: Cilia
structures.evidence: Between 10,000 and 14,000 cilia cover it and beat in waves, pushing it along at about one millimetre per second.

sources.title: Paramecium caudatum: Habitat, Culture, Structure, Locomotion

structures.name: Oral groove
structures.evidence: Cilia sweep bacteria, yeast and algae into its oral groove.

sources.title: Integrative Neuroscience of Paramecium, a "Swimming Neuron"

structures.name: Nucleus
structures.evidence: A moving Amoeba proteus is 160 to 760 micrometres long, with one nucleus 22 to 62 micrometres across.

structures.name: Contractile vacuole
structures.evidence: One contractile vacuole, often near the rear (uroid).

structures.name: Food vacuole
structures.evidence: It is a predator that surrounds bacteria and algae and takes them into a food vacuole.

structures.name: Pseudopodia
structures.evidence: It has no fixed shape and usually pushes out several pseudopodia at once, one bigger than the rest.

structures.name: Flagellum
structures.evidence: A red eyespot sits near the base of the flagellum it swims with.

structures.name: Chloroplasts
